sourceWrites.body:
# symbols.yaml
# AUTHORED fields (edit freely):
#   id, title, sourceFile, links, status, tags, owner, priority
# Coordinates are derived from source by every `kibi sync` into the
# gitignored symbol-coordinates.yaml; they are never authored or committed.
#
# Coordinate refresh granularity gate:
#   The AST extractor locates per-declaration spans for code files. When it
#   cannot find a declaration, a title-match or whole-file coarse span is
#   published ONLY for symbols that declare a coarse granularity_reason
#   (config-artifact, module-level-behavior, extractor-miss, test-suite).
#   A symbol without granularity_reason whose extraction misses gets no
#   coordinate entry at all and is reported as failed; add symbol_role and
#   granularity_reason to opt it into the coarse fallback.
symbols:
  - id: SYM-validate-family-name
    title: validateFamilyName
    status: active
    sourceFile: src/fixture.ts
    relationships:
      - type: covered_by
        target: TEST-fixture-family-handling
      - type: implements
        target: REQ-fixture-family-name-trimming
  - id: SYM-limit-family-name
    title: limitFamilyName
    status: active
    sourceFile: src/fixture.ts
    relationships:
      - type: covered_by
        target: TEST-fixture-family-handling
      - type: implements
        target: REQ-fixture-family-name-length-limit
  - id: SYM-format-family-label
    title: formatFamilyLabel
    status: active
    sourceFile: src/fixture.ts
    relationships:
      - type: covered_by
        target: TEST-fixture-family-handling
      - type: implements
        target: REQ-fixture-family-label-format

properties.title: Fixture family names and labels are handled consistently
Fixture family labels are family: followed by the name

pair_reviews.separated_by: The label format applies to the display label built from a name, while the length limit applies to the name itself before any label is built.
Trimming applies to the incoming name; the label format applies to the label built afterwards from the trimmed name.

properties.title: Fixture family names are limited to 32 characters

pair_reviews.separated_by: Trimming runs first and the 32-character limit is measured on the trimmed name, so the two rules apply in sequence and never disagree.

answer:
REQ-fixture-family-handling is split into one requirement per behavior, as approved in approval-state.json ("Split REQ-fixture-family-handling into one requirement per behavior. Keep my sentences as they are.", 2026-11-12). The unfiltered `kb_check` now reports zero violations, and `broad_requirement_review` is gone.

**What changed**
- `REQ-fixture-family-name-trimming`: "A fixture family name must be trimmed. An empty name must be rejected." Owns `validateFamilyName`, with scenario `SCEN-fixture-family-handling-trim`.
- `REQ-fixture-family-name-length-limit`: "A name must be at most 32 characters. A longer name must be rejected with an error that states the limit." Owns `limitFamilyName`, with scenario `SCEN-fixture-family-handling-limit`.
- `REQ-fixture-family-label-format`: "A fixture family label must be family: followed by the name." Owns `formatFamilyLabel`, with scenario `SCEN-fixture-family-handling-label`.
- Each child supersedes the parent. The sentences are verbatim, and each child has a sectioned body with Context, Why this changed and Source.
- `REQ-fixture-family-handling` is set to `closed`, and its `specified_by` and `implements` links are removed.
- The six delegating symbols (`fixtureFamily`, `fixtureFamilyFromArgs`, `fixtureFamilyFromEnv`, `fixtureFamilyLabel`, `fixtureFamilyLabelFromEnv`, `fixtureFamilyOrDefault`) are deleted through the hash-bound plan. They decided no behavior of their own.

**Not done, and why**
- The three children are agent-authored with `origin.ref` quoting the person's approval. I did not set `origin.approved_by`, because that is the reviewer's field. `kb_check` now lists them as needing human approval.
- The semantic advisor flags every clause as an ontology gap, and the new requirements have no `logic_claims` grounding. I did not model them, so `logical_coverage_review` remains a non-blocking review item. The advisor also suggested a `characters` subject that I did not apply, because its definition is not stated anywhere.
- The three children have only unit-level test coverage, and there is no proof receipt.
- Some writes skipped the dryRun preflight: the symbol relationship updates, the parent close and the wrapper deletion. The first child was dry-run first. The other two were rejected on the first attempt for missing inventory fields, and I fixed those and wrote them without a second dry run.
- Telemetry reports low diagnostic completeness. It is non-blocking.

**Closeout**
- taskOutcome: complete
- kbState: clean_fresh (the post-write check ran against the current snapshot)
- verificationState: not_evaluated (no proof run)
- proofState: unresolved
- limitationDisposition: accepted (the approval gap and the ontology gaps are listed above for review)
